title.zh: 卷257 列傳四十四 赵国祚 许贞 徐治都 唐希顺 赵应奎 李芳述 陈世凯 许占魁
title.en: Volume 257 Biographies 44: Zhao Guozuo, Xu Zhen, Xu Zhidou, Tang Xishun, Zhao Yingkui, Li Fangshu, Chen Shikai, Xu Zhankui
title.raw: 卷257 列傳四十四 赵国祚 许贞 徐治都 唐希顺 赵应奎 李芳述 陈世凯 许占魁

sentences.zh: =趙國祚=趙國祚，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: =Zhao Guozuo= Zhao Guozuo was a man of the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guozuo belonged to the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 父一鶴，太祖時來歸。

translations.literal: His father Yiyihe submitted to the dynasty in the time of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yiyihe came over to the Qing in the Taizu reign.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，授三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: During the Tiancong period he was granted the rank of third-class jala zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancong era he received the third-class company commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 國祚其次子也。

translations.literal: Guozuo was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo was Yiyihe's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授牛錄額真，屯田義州。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed niru ejen and opened military colonies at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made a company captain and put in charge of garrison farming at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 從征黑龍江。

translations.literal: He followed on the campaign against the Heilongjiang region.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the Heilongjiang campaign.

sentences.zh: 取前屯衛、中後所。

translations.literal: He captured Qiantun Guard and the Zhonghou garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: He took Qiantun Guard and the Zhonghou stations.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從征江南，克揚州、嘉興、江陰，皆有功。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi he followed the southern campaign, captured Yangzhou, Jiaxing, and Jiangyin, and distinguished himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he joined the Jiangnan campaign, took Yangzhou, Jiaxing, and Jiangyin, and earned merit in each action.

sentences.zh: 世職自半個前程累進二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: His hereditary office rose from half-rank prospect stipend to second-class adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: His hereditary rank advanced from a half-rank prospect grant to a second-class light-chariot commandancy.

sentences.zh: 歷官自甲喇額真累遷鑲白旗漢軍固山額真。

translations.literal: In office he rose from jala ejen to gushan ejen of the Han Chinese Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks from company commander to banner general of the Han Chinese Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加平南將軍，駐師溫州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made Pacification General of the South and stationed his army at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was promoted to Pacification General of the South and encamped at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授浙江總​​督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became governor-general of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功犯溫州，國祚督兵擊卻之，得舟九十餘。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong attacked Wenzhou; Guozuo led troops to repulse him and captured more than ninety boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Chenggong struck Wenzhou, Guozuo drove him off and seized over ninety vessels.

sentences.zh: 成功又犯寧波，副都統夏景梅、總兵常進功等督兵擊卻之，奏捷，上以成功自引退，疏語鋪張，飭毋蹈明末行間陋習，罔上冒功。

translations.literal: Chenggong again attacked Ningbo; Vice Commander-in-Chief Xia Jingmei, Regional Commander Chang Jingong, and others led troops to repulse him and reported victory. The emperor held that Chenggong had withdrawn of his own accord, that the memorial language was inflated, and admonished them not to follow the late-Ming habit among commanders of deceiving the throne and claiming false merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong struck Ningbo again; Xia Jingmei, Chang Jingong, and others beat him back and reported a victory. The emperor judged that Chenggong had simply withdrawn, rebuked the inflated report, and warned them against the late-Ming practice of deceiving the court with false battle honors.

sentences.zh: 成功旋大舉犯江寧，督兵防禦，事定，部議國祚等玩寇，當奪官，詔改俸。

translations.literal: Chenggong soon mounted a major attack on Jiangning; Guozuo led troops in defense. When the affair was settled, the ministries held that Guozuo and others had been lax toward the enemy and should be stripped of office; an edict reduced their salaries instead.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong then launched a major assault on Jiangning, which Guozuo helped defend. Afterward the ministries ruled that Guozuo and others had been remiss against the rebels and ought to lose their posts; the throne ordered their salaries reduced instead.

sentences.zh: 國祚督浙江四年，頗盡心民事。

translations.literal: Guozuo governed Zhejiang for four years and devoted himself considerably to the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During four years as Zhejiang governor-general he gave real attention to civil administration.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，米值昂，發帑平糶，並移檄鄰省毋遏糶，民以是德之。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, when rice prices were high, he opened the treasury for relief sales and also sent dispatches to neighboring provinces not to block grain sales; the people were grateful for this.
translations.idiomatic: When famine drove rice prices up, he released treasury grain for fair-price sale and urged neighboring provinces not to block grain traffic; the people owed him gratitude for it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調山東，復調山西。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Shandong, then again to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was moved to Shandong, then to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，甄別各直省督撫，國祚以功不掩過，解任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, when governors-general and governors of all provinces were reviewed, Guozuo was dismissed because his faults were not outweighed by his merits.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1, during the review of provincial governors, Guozuo was removed because his faults outweighed his service.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，十三年，起國祚江西提督，駐九江。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year Guozuo was recalled as provincial military commander of Jiangxi and stationed at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui's rebellion broke out, Guozuo was reappointed Jiangxi provincial commander in year 13 and posted at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵入江西境，命移駐南昌。

translations.literal: When Sangui's troops entered Jiangxi, he was ordered to move his headquarters to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui's forces crossed into Jiangxi, he was ordered to shift his headquarters to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠應三桂，亦遣兵犯江西，陷廣信、建昌。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong joined Sangui and also sent troops into Jiangxi, taking Guangxin and Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong sided with Sangui and sent forces into Jiangxi, capturing Guangxin and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 國祚與將軍希爾根、哈爾哈齊督兵赴援，精忠將易明自建昌以萬餘人迎戰。

translations.literal: Guozuo, together with Generals Xiergen and Ha'erhaqi, led troops to the relief; Jingzhong's general Yi Ming came out from Jianchang with more than ten thousand men to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo marched to the rescue with Generals Xiergen and Ha'erhaqi; Jingzhong's general Yi Ming advanced from Jianchang with over ten thousand men to meet them.

sentences.zh: 師分道縱擊，破賊，逐北七十餘裡，克撫州。

translations.literal: The army divided and struck freely, routed the rebels, pursued them north more than seventy li, and took Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing forces split up and routed the rebels, pursued them over seventy li, and recovered Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明復以萬餘人來攻，國祚與前鋒統領沙納哈、署護軍統領瓦岱等奮擊破之，斬四千餘級。

translations.literal: Yi Ming again attacked with more than ten thousand men; Guozuo, with Vanguard Commander Shanaha, Acting Guards Commander Wadai, and others, fought fiercely and defeated them, beheading more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ming returned with another ten-thousand-man assault; Guozuo, Shanaha, Wadai, and others smashed the attack and took more than four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大將軍安親王岳樂請以國祚隨徵，報可。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Grand General Prince An Yuele requested that Guozuo accompany the campaign; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Grand General Prince An Yuele asked that Guozuo join the field army, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，師進攻長沙，三桂兵來犯，國祚擊之敗走。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army advanced on Changsha; Sangui's troops came to attack and Guozuo struck them and put them to flight.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, as the army pressed Changsha, Sangui's troops counterattacked and Guozuo drove them off.

sentences.zh: 尋命移駐茶陵。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to move his station to Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to relocate to Chaling.

sentences.zh: 十八年，長沙下，從安親王攻寶慶。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Changsha fell; he followed Prince An in the attack on Baqing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, after Changsha fell, he followed Prince An against Baqing.

sentences.zh: 世璠將吳國貴據武岡，國祚與建義將軍林興珠督兵力戰，砲殪國貴，克武岡。

translations.literal: Shifan's general Wu Guogui held Wugang; Guozuo and Jianyi General Lin Xingzhu led troops in fierce battle, killed Guogui with artillery, and took Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's general Wu Guogui held Wugang; Guozuo and Lin Xingzhu fought hard, killed Guogui with cannon fire, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 國祚以創發乞休。

translations.literal: Guozuo asked to retire on account of an old wound reopening.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo requested retirement when an old wound flared up again.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，年八十，賜祭葬，諡敏壯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died at the age of eighty; state sacrifices and burial were granted, and he was given the posthumous name Minzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 27 at eighty; the court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Minzhuang.

sentences.zh: 子月襲職，自廣東駐防協領累遷至正紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: His son Yue inherited the office and rose from garrison assistant commandant in Guangdong to lieutenant-general of the Han Chinese Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue inherited the hereditary rank and rose from a Guangdong garrison post to lieutenant-general of the Han Chinese Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: =許貞=許貞，字藎臣，福建海澄人。

translations.literal: =Xu Zhen= Xu Zhen, styled Jinchen, was a native of Haicheng in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhen, courtesy name Jinchen, came from Haicheng in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為鄭氏將。

translations.literal: At first he was a general of the Zheng house.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a commander under the Zheng regime.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，率所部至漳州降，授左都督，駐九江。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he led his command to Zhangzhou to surrender and was appointed Left Commander-in-Chief, stationed at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he brought his troops to Zhangzhou to surrender, was made Left Commander-in-Chief, and posted at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 尋移贛縣，以荒地畀降兵屯墾，號「屯墾都督」。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Gan county, where wasteland was allotted to surrendered troops for garrison farming; he was called the "Colonization Commander-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Gan county, where surrendered troops were settled on wasteland for military farming, earning him the nickname "Colonization Commander."

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，遣其將賈振魯、曾若千犯贛州，陷石城，圍寧都。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled and sent his generals Jia Zhenlu and Zeng Ruoqian to attack Ganzhou, took Shicheng, and besieged Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Geng Jingzhong rebelled; his generals Jia Zhenlu and Zeng Ruoqian struck Ganzhou, seized Shicheng, and besieged Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 廣信、建昌諸山寇應之，州縣多殘破。

translations.literal: Mountain bandits in Guangxin, Jianchang, and elsewhere rose in response, and many districts and counties were ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain rebels across Guangxin and Jianchang joined in, leaving many districts in ruins.

sentences.zh: 貞選所部得健卒四百，會游擊週球赴援，敗賊於黃地，斬級千餘，獲甲幟、砲械無算，遂解寧都圍，复石城。

translations.literal: Zhen selected four hundred stalwart soldiers from his command, joined Guerrilla Commander Zhou Qiu coming to the relief, defeated the rebels at Huangdi, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured armor, banners, and artillery beyond count; he then lifted the siege of Ningdu and recovered Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen picked four hundred of his best men, joined Zhou Qiu's relief force, routed the rebels at Huangdi with over a thousand kills and vast captures of arms, lifted the siege of Ningdu, and retook Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊犯興國，貞馳剿，多斬獲。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Xingguo; Zhen hurried to suppress them and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rebels struck Xingguo; Zhen raced to pursue them and won many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 進攻雩都、瑞金，戰天華山、李芬江、長樂里，屢破賊，克橋頭、五仙、白奇、田產、江頭、上龍、寶石諸寨，降賊萬餘，出難民三萬有奇。

translations.literal: He advanced against Yudu and Ruijin, fought at Tianhua Mountain, Lifen River, and Changleli, repeatedly defeated the rebels, took the stockades at Qiaotou, Wuxian, Baiqi, Tianchan, Jiangtou, Shanglong, Baoshi, and others, received the surrender of more than ten thousand rebels, and freed more than thirty thousand refugees.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed into Yudu and Ruijin, fought at Tianhua Mountain, Lifen River, and Changleli, broke the rebels repeatedly, took a string of stockades including Qiaotou and Wuxian, accepted the surrender of over ten thousand rebels, and freed more than thirty thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 巡撫白色純上其功，詔嘉許，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Governor Bai Sechun reported his merit; an edict praised him and he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bai Sechun memorialized his achievements; the throne commended him and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 總督董衛國請增置撫建廣總兵駐建昌，即以命貞。

translations.literal: Governor-General Dong Weiguo requested the addition of a regional commander over Fu, Jian, and Guang prefectures stationed at Jianchang, and Zhen was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Dong Weiguo asked for a new regional commander for Fu, Jian, and Guang, based at Jianchang, and Zhen received the post.

sentences.zh: 貞督兵复宜黃、崇仁、樂安諸縣。

translations.literal: Zhen led troops to recover Yihuang, Chongren, Le'an, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen recovered Yihuang, Chongren, Le'an, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 精忠使誘貞，貞不發書，械其使以聞，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent envoys to entice Zhen; Zhen would not answer the letter, put the envoys in the cangue and reported it, and was granted the hereditary rank of tosoro hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong tried to win Zhen over by messenger; Zhen ignored the letter, shackled the envoys and reported them, and received a hereditary tosoro hafan rank.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍安親王岳樂駐建昌，精忠遣其將耿繼善、楊玉太、李懋珠等分屯城外麻姑、二聖諸山，岳樂憂之，貞曰：「賊雖多，易與，請先破一砦。

translations.literal: At that time Grand General Prince An Yuele was stationed at Jianchang; Jingzhong sent his generals Geng Jishan, Yang Yutai, Li Maozhu, and others to camp separately on Magu, Ersheng, and other hills outside the city. Yuele was troubled by this. Zhen said, "Though the rebels are many, they are easy to deal with; please let me break one stockade first."
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince An Yuele was then at Jianchang while Jingzhong's generals Geng Jishan, Yang Yutai, and Li Maozhu held the hills around the city. Yuele was uneasy, but Zhen said, "They are numerous but not formidable—let me take one stockade first."

sentences.zh: 」即夕馳攻蕭家坪，破一砦。

translations.literal: " That very night he galloped to attack Xiaojiaping and broke one stockade.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he stormed Xiaojiaping and carried one stockade.

sentences.zh: 岳樂乃督兵自吉安進攻長沙，留滿洲兵五百俾貞守建昌。

translations.literal: Yuele then led the army from Ji'an against Changsha, leaving five hundred Manchu troops for Zhen to hold Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele then marched from Ji'an on Changsha, leaving Zhen five hundred Manchu troops to hold Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 貞所部僅二千，賊诇守兵寡，攻城，分屯城東南從姑山，貞自將銳卒攻之，直上破壘，賊引卻。

translations.literal: Zhen had only two thousand men under him; the rebels scouted and found the garrison thin, attacked the city, and encamped on Congu Mountain southeast of the wall. Zhen personally led crack troops against them, stormed straight up and broke their ramparts, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: With only two thousand men, Zhen faced a rebel probe that found the garrison weak, then a siege with camps on Congu Mountain. He led elite troops uphill, smashed their works, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 麻姑山最峻，賊數万人屯其上，環山立寨。

translations.literal: Magu Mountain was the steepest; tens of thousands of rebels were encamped on it, with stockades built all around the slopes.
translations.idiomatic: Magu Mountain was the steepest strongpoint, where tens of thousands of rebels had ringed the heights with stockades.

sentences.zh: 貞休兵數月，時就山麓操演，賊易之，不為備。

translations.literal: Zhen rested his troops for several months and from time to time drilled at the foot of the mountain; the rebels took him lightly and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rested his army for months while drilling casually at the mountain foot; the rebels grew contemptuous and let their guard down.

sentences.zh: 十五年，春水發，溪澗皆可舟，賊寨隔水為浮橋相屬。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the spring floods rose and streams and ravines could all be navigated; the rebel stockades across the water were linked by floating bridges.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 spring floods made the streams navigable and the rebel camps were joined by pontoon bridges across the water.

sentences.zh: 貞復引兵操山麓，出不意，督兵直上突賊壘，別將舟載薪焚浮橋，一日破六十餘砦，斬其將揭重信等，其眾殲焉。

translations.literal: Zhen again led troops to drill at the mountain foot, then struck unexpectedly, drove his men straight up to storm the rebel ramparts, while another detachment in boats loaded fuel and burned the floating bridges; in one day more than sixty stockades were taken and the generals Jie Zhongxin and others were beheaded; their forces were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again drilled at the foot of the hill, then suddenly stormed uphill while boats burned the pontoon bridges with fire-laden timber; in a single day he took more than sixty stockades, killed Jie Zhongxin and other rebel leaders, and wiped out their force.

sentences.zh: 繼善屯二聖山，餘眾分屯沙坪、紅門、梓木嶺。

translations.literal: Jishan held Ersheng Mountain while the remainder encamped separately at Shaping, Hongmen, and Zimuling.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan held Ersheng Mountain while the rest camped at Shaping, Hongmen, and Zimuling.

sentences.zh: 貞复休兵數月，當暑，督兵出攻，肉薄，陟崖，大破賊。

translations.literal: Zhen again rested his troops for several months; in the heat of summer he led them out to attack, closed at close quarters, climbed the cliffs, and routed the rebels decisively.
translations.idiomatic: After another months-long pause, Zhen attacked in midsummer, closed hand to hand, scaled the cliffs, and broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 繼善棄砦走入杉關，師從之，進克金谿、南豐。

translations.literal: Jishan abandoned his stockade and fled into Shanguan Pass; the army pursued and advanced to take Jinxi and Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan abandoned his camp and fled through Shanguan Pass; the Qing forces followed and took Jinxi and Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 復進克廣昌，攻瀘溪。

translations.literal: They advanced further to take Guangchang and attacked Luxi.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to capture Guangchang and laid siege to Luxi.

sentences.zh: 瀘溪在萬山中，精忠將楊益茂、林鎮等以四萬人守隘，為之柵。

translations.literal: Luxi lay deep in the mountains; Jingzhong's generals Yang Yimao, Lin Zhen, and others defended the pass with forty thousand men and built palisades for it.
translations.idiomatic: Luxi sat deep in the mountains, where Jingzhong's generals Yang Yimao and Lin Zhen held the pass with forty thousand men behind wooden defenses.

sentences.zh: 貞督兵陟嶺，援柵以上，焚其壘，遂克瀘溪。

translations.literal: Zhen led troops up the ridge, pulled themselves up by the palisades, burned the ramparts, and then took Luxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen climbed the ridge, hauled his men up the palisades, burned the works, and took Luxi.

sentences.zh: 懋珠寇南豐，貞赴援，擊賊楊梅岩，斬其將王大耀等，進克新城。

translations.literal: Maozhu raided Nanfeng; Zhen went to the relief, struck the rebels at Yangmeiyan, beheaded their general Wang Dayao and others, and advanced to take Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhu threatened Nanfeng, Zhen marched to its aid, defeated the rebels at Yangmeiyan, killed Wang Dayao and other leaders, and took Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 十六年，懋珠、玉太走入樂安，副都統尼滿、提督趙賴與貞會師進攻。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Maozhu and Yutai fled into Le'an; Vice Commander-in-Chief Niman, Provincial Commander Zhao Lai, and Zhen united their forces for the attack.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Maozhu and Yutai withdrew into Le'an; Niman, Zhao Lai, and Zhen joined forces to attack them.

sentences.zh: 貞出西路，擊賊白石嶺，复樂安。

translations.literal: Zhen marched out by the western route, struck the rebels at Baishiling, and recovered Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen took the western route, defeated the rebels at Baishiling, and recovered Le'an.

sentences.zh: 玉太以六千人來降。

translations.literal: Yutai came to surrender with six thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yutai surrendered with six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 韓大任自吉安走入樂安，貞督兵擊之，遇於跌水嶺。

translations.literal: Han Daren fled from Ji'an into Le'an; Zhen led troops against him and met him at Dieshuiling.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren fled from Ji'an into Le'an; Zhen pursued and met him at Dieshuiling.

sentences.zh: 一日與八戰，走寧都，立木城都湖塹而守。

translations.literal: In one day they fought eight engagements; Daren fled to Ningdu, built a wooden wall and moat at Duhu, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: They fought eight times in a single day before Daren retreated to Ningdu and fortified Duhu with a wooden wall and moat.

sentences.zh: 圍之兩月，大任出走，敗之永豐，又敗之黃塘老虎峒，眾死亡略盡；

translations.literal: After besieging him for two months, Daren broke out; they defeated him at Yongfeng and again at Huangtang Laohudong, until his followers were nearly all dead;
translations.idiomatic: After a two-month siege Daren broke out, was beaten at Yongfeng and again at Huangtang Laohudong, and his force was nearly destroyed;

sentences.zh: 走福建，詣康親王軍前降。

translations.literal: he fled to Fujian and came before Prince Kang's army to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: he fled into Fujian and surrendered to Prince Kang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，逐賊廣昌，破藤吊、楓樹二寨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he drove rebels from Guangchang and broke the stockades at Tengdiao and Fengshu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he cleared rebels from Guangchang and stormed the Tengdiao and Fengshu stockades.

sentences.zh: 二寨地絕峻，貞駐師永安山與相對，發火器遙擊，焚其寨，乃破之。

translations.literal: The two stockades stood on exceedingly steep ground; Zhen stationed his army on Yong'an Mountain opposite them, struck from afar with firearms, burned their camps, and then broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Both stockades sat on sheer heights; Zhen camped on Yong'an Mountain opposite them, shelled them with firearms, burned them out, and took them.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進世職拜他喇布勒哈番，擢撫建廣饒吉南六府提督。

translations.literal: When his merit was recorded, his hereditary rank was advanced to baitaruburu hafan and he was promoted to provincial military commander over the six prefectures of Fu, Jian, Guang, Rao, Ji, and Nan.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his hereditary rank was raised to baitaruburu hafan and he was made provincial commander over Fu, Jian, Guang, Rao, Ji, and Nan.

sentences.zh: 廣信土賊江機、楊一豹以數万人屯江滸山，倚險立木城，四出剽掠。

translations.literal: The local bandits of Guangxin, Jiang Ji and Yang Yibao, with tens of thousands of men held Jianghu Mountain, built a wooden fortress on the heights, and raided in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxin bandit chiefs Jiang Ji and Yang Yibao held Jianghu Mountain with tens of thousands of men, built a wooden fortress on the heights, and raided the countryside.

sentences.zh: 貞與總督董衛國分兵進攻，迭克要隘。

translations.literal: Zhen and Governor-General Dong Weiguo divided their forces to attack and took the key passes one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Governor-General Dong Weiguo attacked in separate columns and seized the key passes in turn.

sentences.zh: 賊退入雞公山、猴子嶺，复襲破之，斬萬六千餘級。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated into Jigong Mountain and Houziling; he attacked again and broke them, beheading more than sixteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Jigong Mountain and Houziling; he struck again, broke them, and took more than sixteen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 一豹走洪山。

translations.literal: Yibao fled to Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao fled to Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，貞复督兵自弋陽雙港進攻，屢挫賊，斬一豹弟一虎及其眾二千四百有奇。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhen again led troops from Yiyang Shuanggang in attack, repeatedly defeated the rebels, and beheaded Yibao's brother Yihu and more than twenty-four hundred of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 Zhen advanced again from Yiyang Shuanggang, repeatedly beat the rebels, and killed Yibao's brother Yihu along with more than twenty-four hundred of his men.

sentences.zh: 機、一豹俱竄走。

translations.literal: Ji and Yibao both fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Yibao both fled.

sentences.zh: 命貞提督江西全省軍務。

translations.literal: Zhen was ordered to take overall military command of all Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in charge of all military affairs in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，逐賊入江滸山，貞诇賊謀夜劫營，令築壘，兵露刃立垣下，別將伏林中。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, pursuing rebels into Jianghu Mountain, Zhen learned by espionage that they planned a night raid on the camp; he ordered ramparts built, had troops stand with bared blades below the wall, and posted another detachment in ambush in the woods.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19, pursuing rebels into Jianghu Mountain, Zhen learned they planned a night assault; he built breastworks, lined bare blades along the wall, and hid troops in the forest.

sentences.zh: 賊至，見垣內刃如林，驚走，伏發，大破之。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived and saw blades like a forest within the wall, they fled in alarm; the ambush sprang and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came, saw a wall of blades, panicked and fled, and were shattered by the ambush.

sentences.zh: 一豹、機亦走福建降。

translations.literal: Yibao and Ji also fled to Fujian and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao and Ji likewise fled to Fujian and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，自陳乞罷，詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized asking to resign; an edict comforted him and bade him remain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he asked to retire; the throne urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣東提督，朝京師，上褒勞備至，加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to provincial military commander of Guangdong; he had audience in the capital, and the emperor praised and rewarded him with exceptional warmth, adding the rank of tosoro hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Guangdong provincial commander; at court the emperor praised him lavishly and added a tosoro hafan rank.

sentences.zh: 貞蒞粵十四年，造哨船，設塘汛，晝夜巡邏，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: During the fourteen years Zhen was in Guangdong he built patrol boats, established coastal guard posts, and patrolled day and night until bandits vanished from the region.
translations.idiomatic: During fourteen years in Guangdong he built patrol craft, set up coastal posts, and patrolled ceaselessly until piracy all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒，贈少傅，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor and granted state sacrifices and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 34 and was posthumously made Junior Tutor with state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 貞和易，謙抑不伐。

translations.literal: Zhen was easy in manner, modest, and did not boast of his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was affable, modest, and never boastful.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴整，戒所部毋淫掠。

translations.literal: He kept his army in strict order and forbade his men looting and rapine.
translations.idiomatic: He kept strict discipline and forbade his troops looting or harming civilians.

sentences.zh: 收城邑，他將議攻山砦，貞曰：「寇亂方烈，民結寨自保，非盡盜也。

translations.literal: After recovering towns, other generals proposed attacking mountain stockades; Zhen said, "The rebellion is still fierce; the people have banded together in stockades for self-protection—they are not all bandits."
translations.idiomatic: When other commanders wanted to storm mountain stockades after towns were recovered, Zhen said, "The rebellion is still raging; many people have merely fortified themselves for safety and are not all bandits."

sentences.zh: 」止勿攻，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: " He stopped the attacks, and very many lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the attacks and spared a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 江西民甚德之。

translations.literal: The people of Jiangxi were deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiangxi held him in deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: =週球=週球，字季珍，江南來安人。

translations.literal: =Zhou Qiu= Zhou Qiu, styled Jizhen, was a native of Lai'an in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiu, courtesy name Jizhen, came from Lai'an in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年武進士，授廣州衛守備，署南贛營都司，管游擊事。

translations.literal: A military jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed garrison commander of Guangzhou Guard, acted as brigade commander of the Southern Gan camp, and handled guerrilla affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 12 military jinshi, he became garrison commander of Guangzhou Guard, acted as brigade commander of the Southern Gan camp, and handled guerrilla duties.

sentences.zh: 石城陷，總兵劉進寶遣球赴援，與貞合兵擊賊寧都。

translations.literal: When Shicheng fell, Regional Commander Liu Jinbao sent Qiu to the relief; he joined Zhen and together they struck the rebels at Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shicheng fell, Liu Jinbao sent Qiu to the relief; he joined Zhen and attacked the rebels at Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 民避亂紅石崖洞，賊積薪洞口，將舉火焚之。

translations.literal: The people had taken refuge from the turmoil in Hongshiya Cave; the rebels heaped fuel at the mouth of the cave and were about to set it ablaze.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians had taken refuge in Hongshiya Cave; rebels piled brush at the mouth and were about to burn them alive.

sentences.zh: 球兵至，賊走，民以得全。

translations.literal: When Qiu's troops arrived the rebels fled, and the people were thus preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's troops arrived in time, the rebels fled, and the refugees were saved.

sentences.zh: 既克石城，復與貞援興國，球破南安土寇，克崇義、上猶境中諸寨，除游擊。

translations.literal: After Shicheng was recovered, he again joined Zhen in relief at Xingguo; Qiu broke the local bandits of Nan'an and took the stockades within Chongyi and Shangyou, and was made guerrilla commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Shicheng was retaken he joined Zhen at Xingguo, broke the Nan'an bandits, took stockades in Chongyi and Shangyou, and was made guerrilla commander.

sentences.zh: 復與游擊李天柱援會昌，破賊。

translations.literal: He again joined Guerrilla Commander Li Tianzhu in relief at Huichang and defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Guerrilla Commander Li Tianzhu to relieve Huichang and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，叛將陳昇引精忠將郭應輔等陷龍泉，球與天柱破黃土關，克龍泉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi the rebel general Chen Sheng led Jingzhong's general Guo Yingfu and others to take Longquan; Qiu and Tianzhu broke Huangtu Pass and recovered Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 the rebel Chen Sheng brought Jingzhong's general Guo Yingfu and others to seize Longquan; Qiu and Tianzhu broke Huangtu Pass and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 逐賊，升自林中出誘戰，伏起，球督兵奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels, Chen Sheng came out from the woods to offer battle as a lure; an ambush rose, and Qiu led his troops in fierce attack and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit, Chen Sheng tried to lure them into an ambush from the woods; Qiu led a fierce charge and smashed the trap.

sentences.zh: 攻左安口，陟自險徑，砲殪升。

translations.literal: Attacking Zuo'ankou, he climbed by a perilous path and killed Sheng with artillery.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuo'ankou he climbed a dangerous path and killed Sheng with cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 十五年，贛州增城守兵，球授參將，管副將事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he reinforced the garrison at Zengcheng in Ganzhou; Qiu was appointed brigade general and acted as deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he reinforced the Zengcheng garrison at Ganzhou; Qiu was made brigade general and acted as deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 被巡撫佟國正檄援信豐，破黃士標、王割耳等。

translations.literal: By order of Governor Tong Guozheng he went to relieve Xinfeng and defeated Huang Shibiao, Wang Ge'er, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched by Governor Tong Guozheng to relieve Xinfeng, he defeated Huang Shibiao, Wang Ge'er, and others.

sentences.zh: 十六年，援會昌，戰五里排。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he relieved Huichang and fought at Wulipai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he relieved Huichang and fought at Wulipai.

sentences.zh: 語詳國正傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in the biography of Guozheng.
translations.idiomatic: The details appear in Guozheng's biography.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: When his merit was recorded, he was made Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 復從貞擊破韓大任。

translations.literal: He again followed Zhen and helped defeat Han Daren.
translations.idiomatic: He again served under Zhen and helped defeat Han Daren.

sentences.zh: 大任既降，球與游擊唐光耀督護降卒至福州。

translations.literal: After Daren had surrendered, Qiu and Guerrilla Commander Tang Guangyao escorted the surrendered troops to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Daren surrendered, Qiu and Guerrilla Commander Tang Guangyao escorted the surrendered troops to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 復被大將軍簡親王喇布檄，以二千人從征湖南，守安仁，援永興，立營雞公山，屢破賊，加右都督。

translations.literal: He was again summoned by Grand General Prince Jian Labu with two thousand men to follow the Hunan campaign, garrisoned Anren, relieved Yongxing, established a camp on Jigong Mountain, repeatedly defeated rebels, and was made Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Labu then summoned him with two thousand men for the Hunan campaign; he garrisoned Anren, relieved Yongxing, camped on Jigong Mountain, won repeated victories, and was made Right Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢太原總兵，進左都督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to regional commander of Taiyuan and advanced to Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he became regional commander of Taiyuan and was advanced to Left Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 調漢中，再調真定。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanzhong and then again to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanzhong, then to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，贈太子少保，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted state sacrifices and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 22 and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: =徐治都=徐治都，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: =Xu Zhidou= Xu Zhidou was a man of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhidou belonged to the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父大貴，事太宗，援牛錄額真，兼工部理事官。

translations.literal: His father Dagui served Taizong, was promoted to niru ejen, and concurrently served as a Board of Works official.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dagui served under Taizong, rose to company captain, and also held a post in the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 師攻錦州，戰松山、杏山，克塔山，取中後所、前屯衛，皆在行間。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Jinzhou, he fought at Songshan and Xingshan, took Tashan, and captured Zhonghousuo and Qiantun Guard—all in the front ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinzhou campaign he fought at Songshan and Xingshan, took Tashan, and captured Zhonghousuo and Qiantun Guard, always in the van.

sentences.zh: 順治間，從征太原，自河南徇江南。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi he followed the campaign against Taiyuan and swept south from Henan into Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shunzhi era he joined the Taiyuan campaign and marched south from Henan into Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部侍郎，兼梅勒額真。

translations.literal: He rose in due course to Vice Minister of Justice and concurrently meile ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Justice and concurrently vice banner commander.

sentences.zh: 駐防杭州，領左翼。

translations.literal: He was stationed on garrison duty at Hangzhou and commanded the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Hangzhou and commanded the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 徇福建，攻海澄，還定舟山。

translations.literal: He campaigned in Fujian, attacked Haicheng, and on returning pacified Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Fujian, attacked Haicheng, and on his return secured Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 累功，授世職三等阿思哈尼哈番，加太子少保。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary rank of third-class ashan han hafan and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For long service he received a third-class ashan han hafan hereditary rank and the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡勤果，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He died; he was given the posthumous name Qinguo and granted state sacrifices and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Qinguo with state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 治都，初授佐領，兼參領。

translations.literal: Zhidou was at first appointed assistant commandant and concurrently deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou was first made assistant commandant and deputy commandant.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，擢直隸天津總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was promoted to regional commander of Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he became regional commander of Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 八年，調湖廣夷陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Yiling in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was transferred to Yiling in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，十三年，陷沅州，治都率師赴援。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year Yuanzhou fell; Zhidou led troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Yuanzhou fell in year 13 and Zhidou marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 時四川文武吏附三桂，叛將楊來嘉、劉之复應之。

translations.literal: At that time civil and military officials in Sichuan sided with Sangui, and the rebel generals Yang Laijia and Liu Zhifu joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials across Sichuan then sided with Sangui, as did rebel generals Yang Laijia and Liu Zhifu.

sentences.zh: 治都妻許聞鄰境兵民皆從逆，權以治都令約束將弁，撫慰士卒，並脫簪珥勞軍。

translations.literal: When Zhidou's wife Xu heard that neighboring troops and people were all joining the rebellion, she provisionally used Zhidou's orders to restrain officers, comforted the soldiers, and removed her hair ornaments to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that neighboring troops and civilians were joining the rebels, Zhidou's wife Xu used his authority to steady the officers, comforted the men, and gave her jewelry to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 會上命治都還守夷陵，來嘉、之復以舟師來攻。

translations.literal: When an order came for Zhidou to return and hold Yiling, Laijia and Zhifu attacked with a fleet.
translations.idiomatic: When orders came for Zhidou to return to Yiling, Laijia and Zhifu attacked by water.

sentences.zh: 治都督兵水陸防禦，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Zhidou commanded troops in defense by land and water and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou defended by land and water and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 來嘉據南漳，分路出犯，治都與襄陽總兵劉成龍會師合擊，所斬殺過半。

translations.literal: Laijia held Nanzhang and sent columns out to raid; Zhidou joined Regional Commander Liu Chenglong and together they struck; more than half the enemy were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Laijia held Nanzhang and raided in columns; Zhidou joined Liu Chenglong, and together they killed more than half the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加左都督。

translations.literal: When his merit was recorded, he was made Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Left Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，來嘉復以舟師來攻，治都循江堵截。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Laijia again attacked by water; Zhidou blocked the river along its course.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Laijia attacked again by river; Zhidou blocked the Yangzi line.

sentences.zh: 總兵廨瀕江，寇舟逼廨，妻許督兵與戰，中砲死。

translations.literal: The regional commander's yamen stood on the riverbank; rebel boats pressed the yamen, and Lady Xu led troops into battle and was killed by artillery.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery stood on the river; rebel boats pressed in, and Lady Xu led troops into battle and was killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 總督蔡毓榮、提督桑額疏聞，具述治都忠奮不顧家狀。

translations.literal: Governor-General Cai Yurong and Provincial Commander Sang'e memorialized the throne, fully describing how Zhidou had been loyal and daring, heedless of his family.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Cai Yurong and Provincial Commander Sang'e reported how Zhidou had fought with loyal abandon for his family.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢提督，以胡世英代為總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to provincial commander; Hu Shiying replaced him as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was made provincial commander; Hu Shiying replaced him as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 賊將王鳳岐據巫山，上命治都戒備。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Fengqi held Wushan; the emperor ordered Zhidou to be on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Wang Fengqi held Wushan, and the emperor ordered Zhidou to prepare against him.

sentences.zh: 治都練水師，修五板船百，令世英領之；

translations.literal: Zhidou trained a naval force and built a hundred five-plank boats, which he put Shiying in command of;
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou trained a river navy, built a hundred five-plank boats, and put Shiying in command of them;

sentences.zh: 而與成龍督兵出歸州、興山、巴東，扼形勢，相機進剿。

translations.literal: while he and Chenglong led troops out through Guizhou, Xingshan, and Badong to seize strategic points and strike when opportunity offered.
translations.idiomatic: he and Chenglong meanwhile led troops through Guizhou, Xingshan, and Badong to seize key ground and strike when the moment came.

sentences.zh: 十九年，師次巫山，來嘉、鳳岐以萬餘人拒守。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the army halted at Wushan; Laijia and Fengqi defended with more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 the army reached Wushan, where Laijia and Fengqi defended with over ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 師奪隘，賊突出，治都揮刃力戰，來嘉棄馬越山走，擒鳳岐，斬三千餘級，克巫山。

translations.literal: The army seized the pass; the rebels rushed out; Zhidou waved his blade and fought fiercely; Laijia abandoned his horse and fled over the mountains; Fengqi was captured; more than three thousand were beheaded; and Wushan was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing forces took the pass; as rebels rushed out Zhidou fought hand to hand; Laijia fled over the mountains, Fengqi was captured, more than three thousand were killed, and Wushan fell.

sentences.zh: 進向夔州，夔州賊將劉之衛、瞿洪昇以城降。

translations.literal: Advancing toward Kuizhou, the rebel generals Liu Zhiwei and Qu Hongsheng surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Kuizhou, rebel generals Liu Zhiwei and Qu Hongsheng surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 叛將譚弘遣其子天秘、族人地晉、地升詣軍前請降，繳敕印。

translations.literal: The rebel Tan Hong sent his son Tianmi and kinsmen Dijin and Disheng to the army to request surrender and handed over his commission and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Tan Hong sent his son Tianmi and kinsmen Dijin and Disheng to surrender and handed over his commission and seal.

sentences.zh: 上命治都還守夷陵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhidou to return and hold Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhidou back to Yiling.

sentences.zh: 弘复叛，陷瀘、敘二州。

translations.literal: Hong rebelled again and took Luzhou and Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong rebelled again and seized Luzhou and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 治都與鎮安將軍噶爾漢督兵溯江上，分軍為三隊擊賊，進克下關城。

translations.literal: Zhidou and Pacification General Garhan led troops upriver, divided the army into three columns to strike the rebels, and advanced to take Xiaguan city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou and Pacification General Garhan advanced upriver in three columns and took Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進向雲陽，屢敗賊。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year they advanced toward Yunyang and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 they advanced on Yunyang and repeatedly defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時弘已死，天秘走萬縣。

translations.literal: By then Hong was already dead and Tianmi had fled to Wan county.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was already dead by then, and Tianmi had fled to Wan county.

sentences.zh: 治都復進复梁山、忠州。

translations.literal: Zhidou advanced again and recovered Liangshan and Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou advanced again and recovered Liangshan and Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進四級。

translations.literal: When his merit was recorded, he was advanced four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was advanced four ranks.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，湖廣督標裁兵夏逢龍作亂，據武昌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Xia Fenglong, a demobilized soldier of the Huguang provincial command, mutinied and seized Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Xia Fenglong, a demobilized soldier of the Huguang provincial command, mutinied and seized Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 治都督兵赴剿，至應城，與賊遇，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Zhidou led troops to suppress them; at Yingcheng he met the rebels and fought fiercely to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou marched to suppress them, met the rebels at Yingcheng, and drove them back in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 遂駐師應城。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 賊萬餘環攻，治都分兵內外夾擊，賊大潰，奔德安。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rebels surrounded and attacked; Zhidou struck from inside and outside; the rebels were routed and fled to De'an.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand rebels besieged him; Zhidou attacked from inside and outside, routed them, and they fled to De'an.

sentences.zh: 逢龍乘北風聯巨艦二十順流下，見治都水師嚴整，不敢攻，乃登龍川磯攻陸師。

translations.literal: Fenglong, riding a north wind, linked twenty great ships and drifted downstream; seeing Zhidou's navy in tight order, he dared not attack and instead landed at Longchuanji to strike the land force.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong sent twenty great ships downstream on a north wind; seeing Zhidou's fleet in good order he avoided it and landed at Longchuanji to attack the army.

sentences.zh: 治都督兵迎擊，晝夜鏖戰，斬殺殆盡。

translations.literal: Zhidou led troops to meet the attack; they fought day and night until the enemy were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidou met him in day-and-night fighting until the rebels were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 逢龍合餘眾泊鯉魚潦，治都令諸將鄭興、楊明錦防賊登陸，而自將水師循江發火器焚賊舟。

translations.literal: Fenglong gathered his remnant at Liyuliao; Zhidou ordered Generals Zheng Xing and Yang Mingjin to guard against a landing while he himself led the fleet along the river, firing ordnance to burn the rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong gathered at Liyuliao; Zhidou posted Zheng Xing and Yang Mingjin against a landing while he burned the rebel fleet with river guns.

sentences.zh: 逢龍再攻陸師，复戰卻之，斬七百餘級，餘多赴水死。

translations.literal: Fenglong attacked the land force again; they fought him off once more, beheaded more than seven hundred, and the rest mostly drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong attacked the land force again and was beaten off with more than seven hundred killed; most of the rest drowned.

sentences.zh: 其將胡耀乾等以武昌降，逢龍走黃州。

translations.literal: His generals Hu Yaoqian and others surrendered Wuchang; Fenglong fled to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Generals including Hu Yaoqian surrendered Wuchang; Fenglong fled to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 振武將軍瓦岱督八旗兵至，黃岡諸生宜畏生擒逢龍以獻，磔於市，亂乃定。

translations.literal: Pacification General Wadai arrived with the Eight Banners; the Huanggang student Yi Weisheng captured Fenglong and presented him; he was dismembered in the market and the turmoil was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification General Wadai arrived with the Eight Banners; student Yi Weisheng of Huanggang captured Fenglong, who was executed in the market and the rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜孔雀翎，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was granted a peacock feather and a hereditary tosoro hafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: On news of victory he received a peacock feather and a hereditary tosoro hafan rank.

sentences.zh: 治都師未還，桃源土寇萬人傑為亂，治都妻孔督兵剿平之。

translations.literal: Before Zhidou's army had returned, the Taoyuan bandit Wan Renjie rose in revolt; Zhidou's wife Kong led troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhidou returned, Taoyuan bandit Wan Renjie rebelled; Zhidou's wife Kong led troops and put him down.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，朝京師，賚御用冠服。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he had audience in the capital and was bestowed imperial robes and headgear.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he had audience in the capital and received imperial robes and headgear.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，詔嘉治都功，用孫思克、施琅例授鎮平將軍，仍領提督事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year an edict praised Zhidou's merit; following the precedents of Sun Sike and Shi Lang he was made Pacification General while still holding the provincial command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 the throne praised his service and, following the precedents of Sun Sike and Shi Lang, made him Pacification General while he retained the provincial command.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，卒，贈太子少保，諡襄毅，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Xiangyi, and granted state sacrifices and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 36, was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, named Xiangyi, and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 治都在湖廣十八年，整飭軍紀，民感其惠，為立祠以祀。

translations.literal: Zhidou was in Huguang for eighteen years, tightened military discipline, and the people were grateful for his kindness; they built a shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: For eighteen years in Huguang he enforced discipline; the people were grateful and built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: =胡世英=胡世英，字汝迪，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: =Hu Shiying= Hu Shiying, styled Rudi, was a native of She county in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shiying, courtesy name Rudi, came from She county in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初從福建總督李率泰軍。

translations.literal: At first he followed the army of Fujian Governor-General Li Shuatai.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Fujian Governor-General Li Shuatai.

sentences.zh: 累功至參將。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he rose to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷湖廣督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was moved to deputy commander of the Huguang provincial command's central brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he became deputy commander of the Huguang provincial central brigade.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢副總兵，守荊州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to vice regional commander and defended Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made vice regional commander and defended Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，總督蔡毓榮檄為中軍。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Governor-General Cai Yurong summoned him as army controller.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Governor-General Cai Yurong summoned him as army controller.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大將軍順承郡王勒爾錦自荊州渡江擊三桂，世英以四百人為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Grand General Prince Shuncheng Leerjin crossed the Yangzi from Jingzhou to strike Sangui; Shiying led four hundred men as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Grand General Prince Shuncheng Leerjin crossed the Yangzi from Jingzhou against Sangui; Shiying led four hundred men as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 師集圍合，賊援至，沖我師，斷為二。

translations.literal: As the encirclement closed, rebel reinforcements arrived, charged the army, and cut it in two.
translations.idiomatic: As the encirclement closed, rebel reinforcements arrived, charged in, and cut the army in two.

sentences.zh: 世英張左右翼略陣，度師已畢濟，乃分騎隊逆戰，人持二炬，賊驚不敢逼，徐引還。

translations.literal: Shiying deployed his left and right wings to steady the line, judged that the army had finished crossing, then divided his cavalry to fight in reverse; each man carried two torches; the rebels were alarmed and dared not press close; he withdrew slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying steadied both wings, saw the army had finished crossing, then sent cavalry to fight a rearguard action with two torches per man; the rebels dared not press close and he withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 十六年，常、澧諸郡飢，三桂將吳應麒屯岳州，糶倉穀以為利。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Changde and Li prefectures suffered famine; Sangui's general Wu Yingqi was encamped at Yuezhou selling granary grain for profit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Changde and Li prefectures suffered famine while Sangui's general Wu Yingqi at Yuezhou sold government grain for profit.

sentences.zh: 世英密令人市焉，白勒爾錦乘賊飢督兵水陸並進。

translations.literal: Shiying secretly sent men to buy it and told Leerjin to take advantage of the rebels' hunger and advance by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying secretly bought the grain and urged Leerjin to advance by land and water while the rebels were hungry.

sentences.zh: 世英為前鋒，棹小舟直抵巴陵，溯風而戰，偪岸且近。

translations.literal: Shiying served as vanguard, poled small boats straight to Baling, fought against the wind, and pressed close to the shore.
translations.idiomatic: As vanguard he poled small boats to Baling, fought against the wind, and closed on the shore.

sentences.zh: 世英呼而登曰：「得城陵磯矣！

translations.literal: Shiying called out as he climbed: "We have reached Chenglingji!"
translations.idiomatic: Climbing ashore he shouted, "We have Chenglingji!"

sentences.zh: 」師畢登，破賊壘。

translations.literal: " The army finished landing and broke the rebel ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The army finished landing and broke the rebel works.

sentences.zh: 十八年，應麒走，城民迎師入。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Yingqi fled and the townspeople welcomed the army in.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 Yingqi fled and the townspeople welcomed the army in.

sentences.zh: 勒爾錦請設隨徵四鎮，世英授後路總兵，尋調夷陵。

translations.literal: Leerjin requested the establishment of four campaign garrisons; Shiying was made rear-route regional commander and soon transferred to Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: Leerjin asked for four campaign garrisons; Shiying became rear-route regional commander and was soon transferred to Yiling.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從治都克巫山，擒鳳岐，進取重慶。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed Zhidou in taking Wushan, capturing Fengqi, and advancing on Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he followed Zhidou in taking Wushan, capturing Fengqi, and advancing on Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 以病還夷陵，未幾卒。

translations.literal: He returned to Yiling on account of illness and died soon after.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yiling ill and died soon after.

sentences.zh: =唐希順=唐希順，甘肅武威人。

translations.literal: =Tang Xishun= Tang Xishun was a native of Wuwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xishun came from Wuwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 自行伍補涼州鎮標把總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was made platoon leader of the Liangzhou garrison brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to platoon leader in the Liangzhou garrison brigade.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，王輔臣叛，希順從總兵孫思克進剿河東，轉戰有功。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when Wang Fuchen rebelled, Xishun followed Regional Commander Sun Sike in suppressing the east bank of the Yellow River and distinguished himself in successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, when Wang Fuchen rebelled, Xishun followed Sun Sike on the east bank of the Yellow River and fought with distinction.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從圍平涼，破賊虎山墩，希順奮勇爭先，手足被傷。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed the siege of Pingliang and broke the rebel position at Hushandun; Xishun strove to be first and was wounded in hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he joined the siege of Pingliang, stormed Hushandun, and was wounded in hands and feet striving to be first.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予參將銜，管提標千總。

translations.literal: When his merit was recorded, he was given the rank of brigade general and commanded a thousand-man company of the provincial brigade.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received brigade-general rank and commanded a provincial-brigade company.

sentences.zh: 尋遷守備，偕參將康調元攻复階州、文縣。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to garrison commander and, with Brigade General Kang Tiaoyuan, recovered Jiezhou and Wen county.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made garrison commander and, with Kang Tiaoyuan, recovered Jiezhou and Wen county.

sentences.zh: 十九年，勇略將軍趙良棟徵四川，調希順從軍，遷四川川北鎮標游擊。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Valiant General Zhao Liangdong campaigned in Sichuan; Xishun was transferred to his army and promoted to guerrilla commander of the northern Sichuan garrison brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Valiant General Zhao Liangdong campaigned in Sichuan; Xishun joined his army and became guerrilla commander of the northern Sichuan brigade.

sentences.zh: 時吳世璠將胡國柱等踞關山大象嶺，良棟軍由雅州進剿，复榮經。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shifan's generals Hu Guozhu and others held Daxiang Ridge at Guanshan; Liangdong's army advanced from Ya prefecture in suppression and recovered Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's generals Hu Guozhu and others then held Daxiang Ridge; Liangdong advanced from Ya prefecture and recovered Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 賊退入箐口驛，分兵扼周公橋、黃泥鋪諸隘，結五營守險。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated into Jingkou Post, divided their forces to hold Zhougong Bridge, Huangnipu, and other passes, and formed five camps to guard the heights.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Jingkou Post, held Zhougong Bridge, Huangnipu, and other passes, and formed five camps on the heights.

sentences.zh: 希順從總兵李芳述及調元等進攻土地橋，連破其壘。

translations.literal: Xishun followed Regional Commander Li Fangshu and Tiaoyuan and others in attacking Tudi Bridge, breaking rampart after rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Xishun followed Li Fangshu and Tiaoyuan in attacking Tudi Bridge and took one rampart after another.

sentences.zh: 抵橋口，選步兵千，由間道穿山箐，自山頂下攻。

translations.literal: Reaching the bridge mouth, he chose a thousand foot soldiers to cross by a path through the mountain ravines and attack from the summit.
translations.idiomatic: At the bridge mouth he chose a thousand infantry to cross by a mountain path and attack from above.

sentences.zh: 會橋口兵夾擊，賊潰​​遁。

translations.literal: When the troops at the bridge mouth struck from both sides, the rebels broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With troops at the bridge striking from both sides, the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 乘夜追襲，次日，复敗賊於黎州，克其城，追至大渡河，奪渡口三，遂復建昌。

translations.literal: Pursuing through the night, the next day they again defeated the rebels at Lizhou, took the city, pursued to the Dadu River, seized three crossings, and then recovered Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing overnight, they beat the rebels again at Lizhou the next day, took the city, reached the Dadu River, seized three crossings, and recovered Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 其冬，從良棟自金沙江下雲南，敗賊於玉皇閣、三市街。

translations.literal: That winter he followed Liangdong down the Jinsha River into Yunnan and defeated the rebels at Yuhuang Pavilion and Sanshi Street.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he followed Liangdong down the Jinsha into Yunnan and defeated rebels at Yuhuang Pavilion and Sanshi Street.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，敘功，予左都督銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when his merit was recorded, he was given the rank of Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 his service won him Left Commander-in-Chief rank.

sentences.zh: 累遷台灣水師副將。

translations.literal: He rose in due course to vice commander of the Taiwan naval force.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commander of the Taiwan naval force.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，擢貴州威寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to regional commander of the Weining garrison in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he became regional commander of the Weining garrison in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，聖祖親征噶爾丹，命希順隸西路進剿。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the Kangxi Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Xishun to serve under the western route in the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 the Kangxi Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Xishun to serve on the western route.

sentences.zh: 自貴州率親丁百，馳抵寧夏。

translations.literal: From Guizhou he led a hundred personal retainers and rushed to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: From Guizhou he led a hundred household troops and hurried to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 大軍已出塞，希順兼程進，與孫思克軍會，破噶爾丹於昭莫多。

translations.literal: The main army had already crossed the border; Xishun pressed on by forced marches, joined Sun Sike's force, and defeated Galdan at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had already marched beyond the frontier; Xishun pressed on by forced marches, joined Sun Sike, and defeated Galdan at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予世職拖沙喇哈番，擢四川提督。

translations.literal: When merit was recorded, he was granted a hereditary tosoro hafan rank and promoted to provincial military commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His service was recognized with a hereditary tosoro hafan rank and promotion to Sichuan provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「川省幅員遼闊，蠻、苗雜處，水陸交錯。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Sichuan is vast in territory, with Miao and other tribes intermixed and land and water routes crossing one another.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Sichuan covers a vast area where tribal peoples are intermixed and land and water routes crisscross.

sentences.zh: 提標三營，請視各省提標例，營設兵八百。

translations.literal: The commander's three battalions should, following the precedent of other provincial commanders' standards, have eight hundred men per battalion.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's three battalions should follow other provinces' precedent of eight hundred men per battalion.

sentences.zh: 川省額兵三萬六千，臣清釐積弊，兵額充足。

translations.literal: Sichuan has an authorized strength of thirty-six thousand troops; Your servant has cleared away accumulated abuses, and the rolls are now full.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's authorized strength is thirty-six thousand; I have cleared accumulated abuses and the rolls are now full.

sentences.zh: 即於原額內酌量營汛緩急抽調。

translations.literal: From within that authorized total he will adjust detachments according to the urgency of each garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: Within that authorized total I will shift detachments according to each post's urgency.

sentences.zh: 提標兵雖他移，餉仍其舊。

translations.literal: Though the commander's troops may be moved elsewhere, their pay shall remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the commander's troops are reassigned, their pay will remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 標下將備等官，材技優長，弓馬嫺熟，又諳蜀中地利。

translations.literal: The commandant-rank officers under the standard are skilled in arms, expert in bow and horse, and also know the terrain of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant-rank officers under my standard excel in arms, are skilled bowmen and horsemen, and know Shu terrain well.

sentences.zh: 請如松潘、疊溪等營保題事例，擇員題補。

translations.literal: Please apply the precedent of Songpan, Dieling, and similar garrisons for recommendation and appointment, selecting men for nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Please follow the Songpan and Dieling garrison precedent of recommending and appointing selected officers.

sentences.zh: 」允之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 打箭爐舊屬內地，上以西藏番部嗜茶，許西藏營官在打箭爐管理土伯特貿易事。

translations.literal: Dajianlu had long been part of the interior; because the Tibetan tribes in Tibet favored tea, Tibetan garrison officers were allowed to manage Tubo trade affairs at Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Dajianlu had long been interior territory; because Tibetans favored tea, Tibetan garrison officers were allowed to manage Tubo trade at Dajianlu.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，營官喋巴昌側集烈為亂，侵據河東烏泥、若泥、嵐州、善慶、擦道諸處，戕明正、長河西土司蛇蠟喳吧。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year the garrison officer Diebachang Zejilie rebelled, seized east of the river Wuni, Ruoni, Lanzhou, Shanqing, Cadao and other places, and killed the Mingzheng and Changhexi tribal chieftains Shela Chaba.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 the garrison officer Diebachang Zejilie rebelled, seized Wuni, Ruoni, Lanzhou, Shanqing, Cadao and other places east of the river, and killed the Mingzheng and Changhexi chieftains Shela Chaba.

sentences.zh: 總督錫勒達奏請移化林營參將李麟督兵捕治。

translations.literal: Governor-General Xileda memorialized asking that Hualin Garrison Assistant Commander Li Lin be moved to lead troops in pursuit and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Xileda asked that Hualin Garrison Assistant Commander Li Lin be moved to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 賊復攻圍烹壩、冷竹關，希順檄各路兵赴化林，密疏聞。

translations.literal: The rebels again besieged Pengba and Lengzhuguan; Xishun ordered troops from all routes to Hualin and sent a secret memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again besieged Pengba and Lengzhuguan; Xishun summoned troops from all routes to Hualin and sent a secret report.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎滿丕統荊州滿洲兵進剿，並詔希順相機行事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Manpi to lead Jingzhou Manchu troops in suppression, and also decreed that Xishun should act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Manpi to lead Jingzhou Manchu troops in suppression and told Xishun to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 蠻兵五千餘，立營十四，在磨西面及磨岡等處。

translations.literal: More than five thousand tribesmen established fourteen camps on the west face of Moxi and at Mogang and other places.
translations.idiomatic: More than five thousand tribesmen set up fourteen camps west of Moxi and at Mogang and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 希順雪夜渡瀘水，分兵三路進攻：一自子牛攻哪吒頂，一自烹壩攻大岡，一自督兵出咱威攻磨西面及磨岡。

translations.literal: Xishun crossed the Lu River on a snowy night and divided his forces in three columns: one from Ziniu against Nazhatuo, one from Pengba against Dagang, and one under his own command from Zawei against the west face of Moxi and Mogang.
translations.idiomatic: Xishun crossed the Lu on a snowy night in three columns: one from Ziniu against Nazhatuo, one from Pengba against Dagang, and one from Zawei against west Moxi and Mogang under his own command.

sentences.zh: 別遣兵自頭道水登山，馳下夾攻。

translations.literal: He separately sent troops to climb the mountain from Toudaoshui and charge down in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent troops up from Toudaoshui to charge down in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 戰五日，各路俱捷，殲蠻兵五千餘，斬喋巴昌側集烈，遂復打箭爐，喇嘛、番民俱降。

translations.literal: After five days of fighting every column was victorious; more than five thousand tribesmen were annihilated and Diebachang Zejilie was beheaded; Dajianlu was recovered and lamas and tribesmen all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After five days every column won; more than five thousand tribesmen were destroyed and Diebachang Zejilie was beheaded; Dajianlu was recovered and lamas and tribesmen all submitted.

sentences.zh: 尋抵木鴉，番目錯王端柱等繳敕印，歸附喇嘛、番民萬二千餘戶。

translations.literal: Soon he reached Muya; tribal head Cuowang Duanzhu and others surrendered their edict seals, and more than twelve thousand lama and tribal households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reached Muya; tribal head Cuowang Duanzhu and others surrendered their seals, and more than twelve thousand lama and tribal households came over.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the throne praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 尋疏陳善後事，並允行。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized on follow-up measures, and these too were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he memorialized on follow-up measures, and these were approved as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以病乞休，命解任調理。

translations.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he petitioned to retire; he was ordered relieved of office to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he petitioned to retire on grounds of illness and was relieved of office to recuperate.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒，予祭葬如製。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died and was granted obsequies and burial according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 47 he died and received state funeral honors by regulation.

sentences.zh: 子際盛，襲職，入籍四川。

translations.literal: His son Jisheng inherited the rank and was registered in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited the rank and was entered in the Sichuan register.

sentences.zh: =李麟=李麟，陝西咸陽人。

translations.literal: =Li Lin= Li Lin was a native of Xianyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was a native of Xianyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 自行伍從勇略將軍趙良棟下雲南。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and followed Valiant General Zhao Liangdong into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks and followed Valiant General Zhao Liangdong into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 敘功，以都司僉書用。

translations.literal: When merit was recorded, he was appointed acting assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed acting assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，從振武將軍孫思克擊噶爾丹於昭莫多，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi he followed Pacification General Sun Sike in attacking Galdan at Jao Modo and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 35 he followed Pacification General Sun Sike against Galdan at Jao Modo and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 累遷四川化林營參將。

translations.literal: He rose in due course to assistant commander of the Hualin garrison in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant commander of the Hualin garrison in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，昌側集烈作亂，麟奉檄移兵渡瀘，招安咱威、子牛、烹壩、魁梧四處。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Zejilie rebelled; Lin received orders to move his troops across the Lu, and pacified Zawei, Ziniu, Pengba, and Kuiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 Zejilie rebelled; Lin moved his troops across the Lu and pacified Zawei, Ziniu, Pengba, and Kuiwu.

sentences.zh: 尋提督唐希順令麟順瀘水至哦可，出磨西面後，夾攻磨岡。

translations.literal: Soon Provincial Commander Xishun ordered Lin along the Lu from Pengba to Eke, to come out behind the west face of Moxi and attack Mogang in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Commander Xishun ordered Lin along the Lu from Pengba to Eke to strike Mogang from behind west Moxi.

sentences.zh: 麟軍夜迷失道，比明，反出磨西面前，遂攻蠻營，奪磨西面。

translations.literal: Lin's army lost their way at night; by dawn they had come out instead before the west face of Moxi and thereupon attacked the tribal camp and seized the west face of Moxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's men lost the road at night; by dawn they had emerged before west Moxi instead, attacked the tribal camp, and took west Moxi.

sentences.zh: 打箭爐平。

translations.literal: Dajianlu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dajianlu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 希順追劾麟避險就易駐咱威，致失烹壩；

translations.literal: Xishun afterward impeached Lin for avoiding danger and choosing ease by staying at Zawei, which caused the loss of Pengba;
translations.idiomatic: Xishun later impeached Lin for avoiding danger and taking the easy post at Zawei, which led to the loss of Pengba;

sentences.zh: 又進兵迷道，誤軍機。

translations.literal: and also for losing the road when advancing, thus missing the military opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: and for losing the road on the advance and missing the military opportunity.

sentences.zh: 詔總督錫勒達及滿丕等訊鞫，以有功免治罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Governor-General Xileda and Manpi and others to investigate and try the case; because of his merit he was exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Xileda, Manpi, and others to investigate; because of his merit he was spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 累擢登州總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to regional commander of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，策妄阿喇布坦擾西藏，命麟選精兵百，自寧夏赴軍前。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year Tsewang Arabtan harassed Tibet; Lin was ordered to select a hundred elite troops and proceed from Ningxia to the front.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 Tsewang Arabtan harassed Tibet; Lin was ordered to pick a hundred elite troops and go from Ningxia to the front.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，詔都統延信為平逆將軍，率兵進藏，以麟參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year an edict appointed Grand Secretary Yanxin Pacification General and ordered him to lead troops into Tibet, with Lin assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 Yanxin was made Pacification General and ordered into Tibet, with Lin to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋令護送第六世達賴喇嘛進藏，至沙克河，賊乘夜襲營，擊敗之，連敗賊於齊諾郭勒、綽瑪喇等處。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to escort the Sixth Dalai Lama into Tibet; at the Shakhe River the enemy raided the camp at night; they were beaten off and the enemy was repeatedly defeated at Qinuogele, Chuomala, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he escorted the Sixth Dalai Lama into Tibet; at the Shakhe the enemy raided by night and were repulsed, then beaten repeatedly at Qinuogele, Chuomala, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 西藏平，麟率兵自拉里凱旋。

translations.literal: When Tibet was pacified, Lin led his troops in triumph from Lhari.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet was pacified, Lin led his troops home in triumph from Lhari.

sentences.zh: 六十年，授陝西固原提督。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was made provincial military commander of Guyuan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 60 he became provincial commander of Guyuan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，遷鑾儀使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Procession.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 1 he was made Director of the Imperial Procession.

sentences.zh: 追敘平藏功，加右都督，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Retrospective merit for pacifying Tibet won him promotion to Right Commander-in-Chief and a hereditary tosoro hafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: Merit for pacifying Tibet was recognized with Right Commander-in-Chief rank and a hereditary tosoro hafan.

sentences.zh: 以老致仕。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: =趙應奎=趙應奎，河南商丘人。

translations.literal: =Zhao Yingkui= Zhao Yingkui was a native of Shangqiu in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yingkui was a native of Shangqiu in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少入伍，從恭順王孔有德徵湖南、廣西，俱有功。

translations.literal: In youth he entered military service and followed Prince Gongshun Kong Youde in campaigns in Hunan and Guangxi, distinguishing himself in both.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered the army and followed Prince Gongshun Kong Youde in Hunan and Guangxi, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 累遷至湖廣施南副將。

translations.literal: He rose in due course to vice commander of Shinan in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commander of Shinan in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂陷長沙，調應奎為江西袁州副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wu Sangui took Changsha; Yingkui was transferred to be vice commander of Yuanzhou in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Wu Sangui took Changsha; Yingkui was transferred to vice commander of Yuanzhou in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 袁州地逼長沙，又有棚寇，與三桂兵句連。

translations.literal: Yuanzhou lay close to Changsha, and there were also shed bandits in collusion with Sangui's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou bordered Changsha closely, and shed bandits were in league with Sangui's troops.

sentences.zh: 應奎以所部兵力弱，斥貲增募，並家丁助戰，擒斬賊渠硃益吾等。

translations.literal: Because his force was weak, Yingkui spent his own funds to raise more men and brought household retainers into the fighting; he captured and beheaded the rebel chieftain Zhu Yiwu and others.
translations.idiomatic: His force was weak, so Yingkui spent his own funds to raise men and brought household troops into battle; he captured and beheaded the rebel chieftain Zhu Yiwu and others.

sentences.zh: 尋自慈化進剿黃塘、楚山、上栗市，屢敗賊。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced from Cihua to suppress Huangtang, Chushan, and Shanglishi, repeatedly defeating the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he advanced from Cihua against Huangtang, Chushan, and Shanglishi and repeatedly defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 總督董衛國請設袁臨鎮，即以應奎為總兵官。

translations.literal: Governor-General Dong Weiguo requested the establishment of the Yuan-Lin garrison, with Yingkui as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Dong Weiguo asked to establish the Yuan-Lin garrison and make Yingkui regional commander.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣賊犯袁州，應奎力守。

translations.literal: Sangui sent rebels to attack Yuanzhou; Yingkui defended it resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui sent rebels against Yuanzhou; Yingkui held firm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其將硃君聘等以數万人自萍鄉來犯，應奎敗之西村，斬萬五千餘級。

translations.literal: Before long his generals Zhu Junpin and others came from Pingxiang with tens of thousands; Yingkui defeated them at Xicun and beheaded more than fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his generals Zhu Junpin and others came from Pingxiang with tens of thousands; Yingkui defeated them at Xicun and took more than fifteen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 分兵趨萬載，斬其將邱以祥等，復其城。

translations.literal: He detached troops toward Wanzai, beheaded the general Qiu Yixiang and others, and recovered the city.
